searchText: Yes I agree with that point, but I was saying that apps on a successful fraud proof L2 can bear the cost of running checkers since they have outside incentives In the same way that we all have incentives (not financially necessarily) to run Ethereum nodes Of course checkers are more complex than nodes, but that's why I focused on apps running these Example: if there's at least one successful exchange (centralized or not), isn't it almost guaranteed that the operators of that exchange would run checkers? Problem still persists on an L2 without a lot of activity though For these, there could be some community-led initiative that runs checkers on every L2 that needs it This is a tragedy of the commons problem. Only one person needs to foot the bill to secure the system, and if everyone assumes someone else is doing it then you can get into a situation where no one is doing it. This makes sense; I'm not too familiar with checkers, but I'm guessing there could be a way to map/crawl them And see which one is active No one has been able to solve this in a censorship resistant and sybil resistant way yet. This is interesting thank you, are you aware of any resources talking about checkers, except the docs of optimism/arbitrum? Nothing specific, sorry. I think there'll be more talk on it where these L2s start allowing fraud proofs I think part of the reason these things calling themselves L2s don't have actual security is partly because it is actually really hard to build correctly. The power, IMO, is sourced from the government and its exclusive right to use force. The wealthy just leverage that to get ahead. If we stop the wealthy (somehow) from leveraging that power, the power will still exist and still be exploited by those who seek to get ahead. At best we can do what Russia or China did and change the demographic who seizes that power from wealthy people to politicians or the military or whatever. If, instead, we take the power away entirely, then there is nothing left to exploit by anyone. do non-interactive fraud proofs reduce the finality time of an optimistic rollup? Not sure if this is what you are looking for, but these were the original docs outlining ORUs https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06441 https://ethresear.ch/t/minimal-viable-merged-consensus/5617
